kind_definitions.requirement: A property the system must have, stated so that a test can decide it. Id prefix names the area (RISK, EXEC, DATA, MODEL, API, SECR, SUP, RES, REL, GOV).
kind_definitions.invariant: A trading invariant that must hold on every path, at all times. Id prefix INV. These are non-negotiable: an invariant may not be waived, and its verification may not be deleted.
kind_definitions.regression: A defect that reached a running system once. Id prefix REG. Its test outlives the fix and is never deleted because the bug is gone.
kind_definitions.security_regression: A security weakness that was once present or once possible. Id prefix SEC. Its test is permanent, so the weakness cannot silently return.

status_definitions.verified: At least one named test file exists on disk and the entry is considered fully covered. No planned_in.
status_definitions.partial: Named tests exist and cover part of the statement. planned_in names the PR that finishes it. This is the honest status for a requirement the tree already touches but does not yet pin down.
status_definitions.planned: No test exists yet. planned_in names the PR that will create one. Naming no test and no PR is not a permitted state.
status_definitions.accepted_gap: A deliberate, attributed, dated decision not to verify. Requires a waiver. Never available to a critical entry.

criticality_definitions.critical: Violation can lose money, leak a credential, or let unreviewed code reach production. Cannot be waived.
criticality_definitions.high: Violation degrades a safety control or hides a failure, without directly moving funds.
criticality_definitions.medium: Violation costs correctness or operability but has a bounded blast radius.
criticality_definitions.low: Violation is a quality or hygiene concern.

test_types.contract: Does an interface behave as promised?
test_types.api: Does the HTTP surface behave and refuse correctly?
test_types.regression: Did an old bug come back?
test_types.verification: Does the implementation satisfy the requirement?
test_types.validation: Does the system solve the intended problem?
test_types.property: Does a general invariant always hold?
test_types.security: Can an attacker violate a security property?
test_types.model: Is ML inference or training correct?
test_types.signal: Does the strategy generate the intended signal?
test_types.performance: Is it fast and stable enough?
test_types.chaos: Does it fail safely under disruption?
test_types.mutation: Would the suite notice if the logic were subtly wrong?

entries.title: No order exceeds the configured maximum notional
entries.statement: For every order the system submits, notional <= the configured ceiling for that symbol and account, with no path that bypasses the check.

verification.note: Pins the ceiling at the boundary, proves no otherwise-passing input talks the stack past it, and states the sizer-cap versus gate-authority relationship.
Caps the Kelly sizer's notional.
Caps the CVaR path.

entries.failure_mode: A single mis-sized order puts more capital at risk than the risk policy permits.

entries.title: No new entry while a capital-preservation halt is active
entries.statement: While the capital-preservation floor is breached, no new entry order may be produced by any strategy, engine or manual path.

verification.note: Halts at the threshold, never auto-clears on recovery, only re-authorisation lifts it, and it is evaluated first so the audit trail names the right control.
Covers the floor's own decision.

entries.failure_mode: The bot keeps trading through the drawdown it was supposed to stop at.

entries.title: Unknown exchange order state cannot become FILLED without reconciliation
entries.statement: An order whose exchange status is unknown, missing or unparseable is never transitioned to FILLED; it enters a reconciliation state instead.

verification.note: There is no mapping from UNKNOWN to any FSM state, so an unrecognised status cannot become FILLED however the caller is written.
No terminal state can reach FILLED, and PENDING cannot jump past the FILLING confirmation step.

entries.failure_mode: The bot books a fill that never happened, and every downstream position figure is wrong.

entries.title: NaN or Infinity cannot produce an executable order
entries.statement: Any non-finite value reaching price, quantity, notional, confidence or a risk scalar results in refusal, never in an order.

verification.note: Walks NaN and both infinities through every sizer, every gate and the assembled stack, and pins the two documented fail-open exceptions.
Covers the gate stack.

entries.failure_mode: A NaN propagates through sizing and an order of undefined size is submitted.

entries.title: A disabled trading mode cannot submit orders
entries.statement: When live trading is disabled, no code path reaches the live exchange client, including scheduled jobs, retries and reconciliation.

verification.note: The live gate refuses live until both models validate, the paper executor has no import or attribute reaching a venue, and every non-paper mode is gated by default.

entries.failure_mode: The bot trades real money while the operator believes it is in paper mode.

entries.title: Risk engine failure cannot result in an executable order
entries.statement: If the risk engine raises, times out or is unavailable, the decision is NO TRADE. There is no default-allow path.

verification.note: The drift gate fails closed on any exception; a raising gate propagates rather than becoming a pass; no except block in src/risk swallows into a default-allow.
Covers gate outcomes.

entries.failure_mode: An exception in the safety layer silently removes the safety layer.

entries.title: Duplicate execution requests cannot create duplicate positions
entries.statement: Two execution requests carrying the same idempotency key produce at most one exchange order and one position change.

verification.note: Deterministic keys that do not collide across intents, a registry that refuses a replay, and 25 racing reservations that yield exactly one submission.

entries.failure_mode: A retry doubles the position and the account is twice as exposed as intended.

entries.title: A stale market-data sample cannot be treated as current
entries.statement: A sample older than the declared freshness budget is not used for a trading decision unless an explicit, named policy permits it.

verification.note: Staleness measured against a declared budget, with the budget named in the rejection.
Golden case ETHUSDT_15m_case_003: a well-formed frame that stopped updating an hour ago is refused, and no risk decision is reached.
Exercises the quality gate.

entries.failure_mode: The bot trades a price that no longer exists.

entries.title: Position and account state after restart reconcile with the exchange
entries.statement: After any restart, the reconstructed position and balance state matches the exchange's, or the system halts rather than trading on a guess.

verification.note: Reconstructed state is compared against the venue at every crash point; signed quantities, partial fills and dust are each distinguished from a missing position.

entries.failure_mode: The bot restarts believing it is flat while holding a real position, and hedges nothing.

entries.title: Live mode cannot bypass qualification gates
entries.statement: Enabling live trading requires every qualification gate to have passed; no configuration flag, environment variable or API call skips one.

verification.note: LiveExecutor asserts qualification before building any state; the gate takes no override parameter, reads no environment variable, and re-evaluates the stored measurements rather than trusting the stored verdict.

entries.failure_mode: Untested strategy code reaches real capital.

entries.title: check_import_cycles has a negative test
entries.statement: The static invariant that refuses module-level import cycles carries a dedicated fake-tree test proving it can fire on a 2-module cycle, and a companion test proving a deferred (function-scope) import is not counted.
entries.failure_mode: check_import_cycles is reached only by the whole-repo positive gate. A bug that stops it from detecting cycles would ship silently, and a module-level cycle would then fail at collection time with only the ImportError as the signal.

entries.title: Maximum position exposure must not exceed the configured ceiling
entries.statement: For every symbol and for the portfolio as a whole, exposure stays at or below the configured ceiling under every sizing path, including manual overrides.

verification.note: The composition: the sizer's cap is 25% of capital, the gate's ceiling is 5%, and the gate is the authority.
Just inside, exactly on, and just outside the position-size limit.

entries.failure_mode: One oversized position turns a normal drawdown into an account-ending one.

entries.title: Boundary values at every risk limit are exercised
entries.statement: Each configured risk limit has tests at limit-epsilon, limit, and limit+epsilon, so an off-by-one comparison cannot pass.

verification.note: Nine limits, three cases each, with the inclusive or exclusive side of every comparison named in the test name and tabulated in the module docstring.

entries.failure_mode: A `<` written where `<=` was meant permits exactly the trade the limit exists to stop.

entries.title: Position size is non-negative and bounded
entries.statement: For arbitrary generated inputs, the sizer returns a value in [0, limit] or refuses; it never returns a negative, non-finite or unbounded size.

verification.note: Seeded generation over pools weighted toward the values that break comparisons: finite, non-negative and under the ceiling for every sizer and for the combined recommendation.

entries.failure_mode: A negative size inverts the intended direction of the trade.

entries.title: Probabilities and confidences stay within [0, 1]
entries.statement: Every value the system treats as a probability is in [0, 1] where it is consumed, or is rejected at the boundary.

verification.note: An out-of-range probability refuses rather than saturating to the largest permitted bet, and the Bayesian shrinkage primitive guarantees its own output is a probability.

entries.failure_mode: A confidence of 4.0 multiplies position size by four.

entries.title: No optimizer may directly modify a live risk control
entries.statement: Self-tuning output reaches live risk parameters only through bounds, offline evaluation, out-of-sample check, risk tests, shadow, paper and an approval -- never directly.

verification.note: Bounds are checked before quality, so an excellent out-of-bounds proposal is refused before its improvement is weighed; a regression anywhere blocks promotion, and the optimizer cannot reach an executor.

entries.failure_mode: An optimizer relaxes the very limit that would have stopped its own bad idea.

entries.title: Mutation score on the risk subsystem is at or above 90%
entries.statement: Nightly mutation testing of the risk modules kills at least 90% of generated mutants.

verification.note: The 90% risk and sizing floors are declared, every target exists on disk, a run with no mutants is not a pass, and a timeout counts against the score.

entries.failure_mode: High line coverage hides a suite that would not notice if a comparison flipped.

entries.title: Execution requests carry an idempotency key end to end
entries.statement: Every execution request carries a key derived from its decision, and the executor refuses to act twice on the same key.

verification.note: The key travels to the venue as a client order id, and only a provably-unsent request releases it -- a timeout keeps it claimed.

entries.failure_mode: A network retry becomes a second real order.

entries.title: The order state machine is total and its transitions are legal
entries.statement: Every (state, event) pair has a defined outcome, and no transition outside the declared table is reachable.

verification.note: The entire cross product of states and targets, each cell either a permitted transition or a refusal that leaves the state untouched.

entries.failure_mode: An unhandled exchange event leaves an order in a state nothing knows how to close.

entries.title: Exchange responses are validated against a declared contract
entries.statement: Every exchange response is parsed against a schema; unknown, missing or malformed fields produce an explicit failure, not a default.

verification.note: A total parse: every input yields an answer, and one the contract cannot vouch for reports needs_reconciliation rather than a plausible default.

entries.failure_mode: A changed exchange field silently reads as zero and the bot mis-books a fill.

entries.title: Unknown exchange order status must never be treated as FILLED
entries.statement: An unrecognised status string maps to an explicit UNKNOWN outcome that triggers reconciliation, never to a terminal success.

verification.note: An unrecognised status maps to UNKNOWN, and an unknown status carrying an otherwise perfect fill still reconciles rather than booking it.

entries.failure_mode: Position accounting diverges from the exchange without anything reporting an error.

entries.title: The kill switch is authenticated, authorized, audited, idempotent and durable
entries.statement: Activating the kill switch requires an operator role, writes an audit event, is safe to repeat, blocks new entries immediately, and survives restart.

verification.note: Durability: the halt is persisted atomically and restored at startup; a missing file means a first start, an unreadable one resolves to the most restrictive mode.
The halt as an API control: authenticated, authorized by role, and idempotent when repeated.

entries.failure_mode: The control of last resort is unavailable exactly when it is needed.

entries.title: Partial fills and fees are accounted exactly
entries.statement: Position, average price, fee and realised PnL after a sequence of partial fills match a hand-calculated fixture.

verification.note: Hand-calculated volume-weighted averages, including the arithmetic mean stated explicitly as the wrong answer, and 200 fills checked against an independent Decimal accumulation.

entries.failure_mode: PnL is wrong, so every downstream risk decision is made on false numbers.

entries.title: Mutation score on the execution subsystem is at or above 90%
entries.statement: Nightly mutation testing of the execution modules kills at least 90% of generated mutants.

verification.note: The execution subsystem's 90% floor, mutating order_fsm, idempotency and exchange_contract nightly.

entries.failure_mode: The FSM tests assert shape without asserting behaviour.

entries.title: Market data failing the quality gate never reaches the signal engine
entries.statement: Schema, timestamp validity, monotonicity, freshness, OHLC consistency, non-negative volume, and absence of NaN/Infinity are all checked before use; failure means NO TRADE.

verification.note: Every line of the source document's checklist, asserted on the rejection reason as well as on pass/fail.
Golden case ETHUSDT_15m_case_002: one impossible bar refuses the frame before the feature pipeline is reached.

entries.failure_mode: A corrupt bar becomes a signal, and the signal becomes an order.
entries.notes: The gate existed and was tested from the day it was written, but no module in src/ ever called it -- so the statement above was false of the running system until PR-003 wired it into SignalEngine.tick.

entries.title: Data freshness budgets are declared and enforced
entries.statement: Every market-data consumer declares a maximum age, and a sample past it is refused rather than used.

verification.note: FreshnessBudget.for_timeframe derives the budget from the bar interval; the rejection names the budget that refused it.

entries.failure_mode: A frozen feed looks like a calm market.

entries.title: A single clock policy: internal timestamps are UTC and exchange skew is bounded
entries.statement: All internal timestamps are timezone-aware UTC; exchange-versus-local skew beyond the declared bound is detected and reported.

verification.note: Naive datetimes refused rather than assumed, other zones converted rather than relabelled, the DST gap and repeated hour shown to be absent in UTC, and venue skew measured against a declared budget.

entries.failure_mode: A DST shift or a naive datetime silently moves a bar an hour.

entries.title: Money arithmetic uses a declared exact representation
entries.statement: Where money is added, compared or rounded, the representation is documented and exact; float is used only where the doc says it may be.

verification.note: The declared policy is float64 with Decimal at the exchange-precision boundary; quantisation never rounds up, accumulated drift over a day of fills stays inside 1e-9 relative, and the percent-versus-fraction units are pinned.

entries.failure_mode: Rounding drift accumulates until the ledger and the exchange disagree.
entries.notes: The representation is float64, not Decimal, and docs/quality/MONEY_AND_TIME.md argues for that rather than claiming otherwise. It also records the conditions under which the decision should be re-argued.

entries.title: Tick size, lot size and minimum quantity are respected
entries.statement: Every submitted order conforms to the venue's tick, lot and minimum-notional rules, checked before submission.

verification.note: Quantisation never increases a quantity, and every minimum is compared against the quantised value -- the number the venue actually sees.

entries.failure_mode: Orders are rejected by the venue at exactly the moment the strategy needs them.

entries.title: Portfolio-level exposure, correlation and agreement limits are enforced
entries.statement: Aggregate exposure, cross-strategy correlation and portfolio agreement are evaluated before an order is sized, and a breach reduces or refuses the order rather than being reported after the fact.

verification.note: Both scalars asserted on the notional that reaches the sizer rather than on the number the tracker reports, and the small-sample shrinkage pinned as intended behaviour rather than discovered as a surprise.

entries.failure_mode: Five uncorrelated-looking positions turn out to be one position in five costumes.

entries.title: Golden signal fixtures pin end-to-end behaviour
entries.statement: Named fixtures carry market input, features, regime, model output, signal, risk decision and expected final action, and CI fails on any unexplained change.

verification.note: Six cases covering clean long, clean short, flat signal, regime halt, corrupt data and stale data. Also asserts the fixture set has not become trivial, which a round-trip check alone cannot see.

entries.failure_mode: A refactor changes what the bot trades and nobody notices until the PnL does.
entries.notes: The model's p_long is supplied by the case rather than computed: a retrained tree on a different library build produces different probabilities, so pinning it would fail for reasons unrelated to this project. Everything downstream of it is real production code.

entries.title: Feature computation is deterministic and reproducible
entries.statement: The same input bars produce bit-identical features across runs and processes.

verification.note: Same process, different process (two subprocesses with deliberately different PYTHONHASHSEED), and prefix stability when later bars arrive.

entries.failure_mode: A backtest cannot be reproduced, so a result cannot be trusted.

entries.title: Mutation score on the signal subsystem is at or above 85%
entries.statement: Nightly mutation testing of the signal modules kills at least 85% of generated mutants.

verification.note: The signal subsystem's 85% floor.

entries.failure_mode: Signal tests assert that something was produced, not that it was right.

entries.title: Every model artifact carries full provenance
entries.statement: A model artifact records model id, training-data hash, feature-schema hash, code commit, hyperparameters, seed, library versions, metrics, validation methodology and artifact hash.

verification.note: All ten fields, with each hash asserted to change when its subject changes and not to change when something irrelevant does.
The manifest written by save() carries a complete record, and the legacy {file, sha256} keys still verify.

entries.failure_mode: A model in production cannot be traced to the data or code that made it.

entries.title: A model never decides to bypass the risk gate
entries.statement: Model output reaches an order only through SIGNAL -> RISK ENGINE -> EXECUTION POLICY; no module lets a model result skip the deterministic safety layer.

verification.note: Behavioural (confidence is not an input to any gate) and structural (no model or intelligence module imports an executor, and the engine does not discard the gate verdict).

entries.failure_mode: A confident model overrides the control designed to survive a confident model being wrong.

entries.title: No lookahead: a signal at T is invariant to data after T
entries.statement: For a dataset truncated at T and the same dataset extended with arbitrary future data, the signal computed at T is identical.

verification.note: The detector is first shown to catch four deliberate leaks and to clear an honest feature, then run against the real pipeline with both real and absurd future data.

entries.failure_mode: The backtest is a fantasy and the live strategy loses money the simulation never showed.

entries.title: Model drift beyond threshold demotes the model
entries.statement: Feature, prediction, confidence, regime, calibration, performance and missingness drift are monitored; breaching a threshold moves the model to degraded/shadow rather than continuing to trust it.

verification.note: A healthy model is not demoted, too little evidence is not drift, a degraded model halts the live track only, and a detector that cannot run fails closed.

entries.failure_mode: The model keeps trading a regime it was never trained on.

entries.title: Model artifacts round-trip and reproduce
entries.statement: Each registered model can be loaded, predicted from, serialised, deserialised and reproduced to the recorded metrics from the recorded seed.

verification.note: Load, predict, serialise, deserialise and reproduce bit-for-bit; a tampered artifact, a missing manifest and a swapped manifest are all refused.

entries.failure_mode: A model that cannot be reloaded cannot be rolled back to.

entries.title: Research output cannot change production parameters directly
entries.statement: A notebook or research script has no path to production trading parameters; promotion runs RESEARCH -> candidate -> validation -> shadow -> paper -> production.

verification.note: The gauntlet is a conjunction with no partial credit, shadow evaluation is a time window a challenger cannot buy its way past, and no tuning or upgrade module imports an executor.

entries.failure_mode: An experiment becomes the production strategy by accident.

entries.title: Cross-validation respects time and purging
entries.statement: Model validation uses combinatorial purged cross-validation with an embargo, so adjacent-sample leakage cannot inflate the reported score.

verification.note: Train and test never overlap, the purge gap before and the embargo after every test block are empty, and the fold count is the binomial coefficient rather than a single pass.

entries.failure_mode: A leaky validation split reports skill the strategy does not have.

entries.title: The authorization matrix is executable and every cell is tested
entries.statement: For each (role, endpoint) pair the declared allow/deny outcome is asserted by a test, including the anonymous row.

verification.note: Every (role, endpoint) cell asserted, including the anonymous row and the escalation direction.

entries.failure_mode: A readonly token places a trade.

entries.title: No insecure direct object references
entries.statement: A caller cannot read or modify another principal's resource by substituting an identifier.

verification.note: Identifiers are validated before any lookup, and every negative outcome returns one indistinguishable body.

entries.failure_mode: One authenticated user reads or cancels another's orders.

entries.title: Injection payloads are rejected at the boundary
entries.statement: SQL, NoSQL, command, template, path-traversal, header and JSON-manipulation payloads are refused wherever input reaches a database, filesystem, subprocess, external API or log.

verification.note: Injection payloads refused at the parsers, the outbound surface and the header boundary.

entries.failure_mode: An attacker reads or rewrites the trading database.

entries.title: Outbound URL handling is SSRF-resistant
entries.statement: Any caller-influenced outbound request refuses localhost, loopback, link-local, private ranges, cloud metadata endpoints and internal hostnames.

verification.note: Every resolved address is checked, the metadata service and private ranges are denied, and the guard is wired into the outbound client.

entries.failure_mode: The bot becomes the attacker's proxy into the private network and the metadata service.

entries.title: WebSocket payloads are validated regardless of connection state
entries.statement: An established connection confers no trust: every message is authenticated, schema-validated, size-bounded, rate-limited and replay-checked.

verification.note: Every inbound frame is size-bounded, schema-validated, freshness-checked, rate-limited and replay-checked, in that order, with one guard per connection.
The upgrade itself is authenticated before any state is touched.

entries.failure_mode: A single authenticated socket becomes an unauthenticated command channel.

entries.title: Rate limiting protects authentication, trading and expensive endpoints
entries.statement: Login, authentication, trade endpoints, sensitive mutations, WebSocket connections and expensive queries are rate-limited, and the limits are tested under burst and sustained load.

verification.note: Rate limiting on the authentication, trading and diagnostic endpoints, keyed per client rather than globally.

entries.failure_mode: An attacker with a valid token issues thousands of orders before anything notices.

entries.title: Security headers are present and correct
entries.statement: Responses carry the declared security headers, and a test fails if one is removed.

verification.note: Each declared header is applied, HSTS only over TLS, and the middleware sits outermost so an error response still carries them.

entries.failure_mode: A browser-side weakness that the headers would have closed.

entries.title: A failing security control never opens a trading endpoint
entries.statement: If authentication, authorization, rate limiting or logging is unavailable, the trading endpoints refuse rather than degrade to open.

verification.note: A control that never reported counts as degraded, any single degradation closes the trading endpoints, and the read-only endpoints stay open by design.

entries.failure_mode: An outage in the auth dependency turns the trade endpoint anonymous.

entries.title: Error responses leak neither secrets nor internals
entries.statement: No error path returns a credential, token, stack trace or internal hostname to a caller.

verification.note: Tracebacks, connection URIs, internal hosts and echoed validation input are all replaced, while the endpoints' own messages survive.

entries.failure_mode: A 500 hands the attacker the next step.

entries.title: Secrets never appear in source, images, logs or workflow YAML
entries.statement: Deliberately triggering errors that involve an API key, secret, JWT, database password, authorization header or exchange credential produces output containing none of them.

verification.note: Provokes the leak rather than asserting its absence: keys, connection URIs, JWTs and private keys are pushed through the log processor and through rendered exceptions.

entries.failure_mode: The exchange key is in a log file that gets shipped to a third-party log service.

entries.title: Secret comparisons are constant-time
entries.statement: Every comparison of a token, signature, key or password uses a constant-time primitive, and a test detects a reversion to `==`.

verification.note: The helpers delegate to hmac.compare_digest, and a source-tree scan asserts no secret-named value is compared with == anywhere in src/.

entries.failure_mode: A timing oracle recovers a token one byte at a time.

entries.title: Keys are environment-separated and rotatable, and rotation is tested
entries.statement: Development, test, paper and production keys are distinct; rotation for normal, compromise, departure, server-compromise, exchange-incident and GitHub-compromise cases is documented and exercised.

verification.note: One master seed still yields distinct material per environment and per exchange; rotation advances generations, and compromise and departure revoke the previous one immediately.

entries.failure_mode: A procedure nobody has run fails on the day it is needed.

entries.title: The audit log is a verifiable hash chain
entries.statement: Each event hashes its own content plus the previous event's hash; modifying, deleting or reordering any event fails verification.

verification.note: Each tampering is performed and then detected: edited field, recomputed hash, deletion, reordering, splice. Tip truncation and the eviction window are stated as the limits they are.

entries.failure_mode: An attacker who reaches the host edits the record of what they did.

entries.title: Signed requests reject tampering and replay
entries.statement: A correct signature is accepted; a modified request, timestamp or parameter is rejected; a replayed request is rejected where the protocol allows it.

verification.note: Tampering with any signed field breaks verification; stale, post-dated and replayed requests are refused by ReplayWindow, and an unverifiable signature never reaches its cache.

entries.failure_mode: A captured order request is replayed to double a position.

entries.title: TLS is verified everywhere and never disabled to make a test pass
entries.statement: HTTPS, secure WebSocket and TLS database connections are required; expired certificates, hostname mismatch, weak protocols, broken chains and plaintext endpoints are detected; no code path disables verification.

verification.note: Cleartext destinations are refused except loopback, and a scanner asserts no source file spells verify=False, ssl=False, CERT_NONE, tlsInsecure or their relatives.

entries.failure_mode: An on-path attacker rewrites market data or order responses.

entries.title: Cryptographic randomness comes from the OS CSPRNG
entries.statement: Nonces, keys, tokens and identifiers that must be unpredictable come from `secrets`/`os.urandom`, never from `random`.

verification.note: Every unpredictable value comes from secrets, a short request is refused rather than quietly served, and src/security never imports random.

entries.failure_mode: A predictable token is guessable.

entries.title: No custom cryptographic primitives
entries.statement: The application calls established libraries; it does not implement its own cipher, hash construction, KDF or signature scheme for security purposes.

verification.note: Each security module delegates to cryptography, hmac, hashlib or secrets; no hand-rolled cipher, key schedule or comparison loop, and mathcore is kept out of the security path.

entries.failure_mode: A homemade primitive fails in a way only an attacker notices.

entries.title: Sensitive data at rest is encrypted, and the key is managed separately
entries.statement: Database backups, production databases, sensitive model artifacts, audit archives and configuration backups are encrypted, with keys held outside the encrypted store.

verification.note: AES-256-GCM round trip, and the restore path under every failure that has caused a real outage: wrong key, truncation, flipped byte, wrong version, mismatched associated data -- all one exception type.

entries.failure_mode: Ciphertext and key are stolen together and the encryption bought nothing.

entries.title: The exchange key the bot holds cannot withdraw
entries.statement: The documented and verified key posture is trading-only, withdrawal-disabled, IP-restricted where supported, with separate paper and production keys on separate subaccounts.

verification.note: A withdrawal-capable or undeclared posture is refused, the shipped declaration is checked, and LiveExecutor asserts it before building any state. The live-venue verification remains a documented human step.

entries.failure_mode: A compromised host becomes a withdrawal, not just a bad trade.

entries.title: Deposit-address derivation cannot produce or accept a private key
entries.statement: src/mathcore/derivation/bip32.py derives extended public keys only. It refuses hardened indices, refuses an extended private key by name, and exposes no function or dataclass field that could hold private key material -- a property asserted structurally by inspecting every public signature, not only behaviourally.
entries.failure_mode: Spending authority present in the process that generates deposit addresses. A trading host is internet-facing and runs untrusted market data through itself; an attacker who reads its memory should learn which addresses to watch and nothing that moves funds. The specific BIP-32 trap is that an extended public key plus any one non-hardened child private key yields the parent private key by subtraction, and therefore the whole branch -- so a module that held both at once would hand over the tree.

entries.title: Derived addresses match what a BIP-32 wallet derives, checked against an independent oracle
entries.statement: Watch-only public derivation agrees with private derivation from the published seed for every non-hardened path tested, and each published master xpub the tests rely on is verified to be what its published seed actually derives rather than trusted as transcribed. Base58Check is validated on parse, so a mistyped extended key is refused instead of decoding to a different valid-looking key.
entries.failure_mode: Deposit addresses that no sender ever pays. A derivation that is self-consistent but disagrees with the standard -- an uncompressed point in the HMAC input, the chain code taken from the wrong half of the digest, a missing reduction mod n -- produces a tree that looks correct in isolation and matches no other wallet. Verifying against a transcribed expected string does not catch it either: one such string was misremembered while writing these tests, which is how the checksum requirement was found.

entries.title: The threshold module supplies sharing primitives and refuses to be a signer
entries.statement: src/mathcore/derivation/threshold.py exposes Feldman commitments, group and participant public keys, share verification, Lagrange weights at zero and dispute evidence, and exposes no function for nonce generation, nonce aggregation, challenge computation or partial-signature combination. The absence is asserted by inspecting every public function name, and the module holds no random source -- the caller supplies the polynomial coefficients.
entries.failure_mode: An ad-hoc threshold Schnorr scheme assembled in-house from correct parts. The Wagner ROS attack forges a signature across many concurrently-opened signing sessions, so the aggregation is broken even though every primitive it is built from verifies in isolation -- which is the most dangerous shape a crypto library can have, because nothing fails a test. The defence is a scheme with a proof of concurrent security (FROST, RFC 9591, or MuSig2), so the pieces are deliberately left unassembled and a test fails if a signing-shaped function appears.

entries.title: A tampered share is rejected and too few shares are refused, not approximated
entries.statement: verify_share checks a share against the dealer's commitments and rejects any value that is not the committed polynomial evaluated at that participant's identifier, including a share valid at a different identifier or under a different dealer. Reconstruction refuses fewer shares than the threshold and refuses duplicate identifiers rather than interpolating an under-determined polynomial.
entries.failure_mode: A custody key that cannot be reconstructed at the moment funds must move, or one reconstructed to the wrong value. A tampered or mis-delivered share surfaces only at reconstruction unless it is verified on receipt; and interpolating fewer than the threshold number of points returns a number indistinguishable from the real secret, so a caller who passes three shares from two distinct holders would sign with a key nobody controls and nothing in the arithmetic could notice.

entries.title: Every workflow declares least-privilege permissions
entries.statement: Each workflow sets `permissions:` explicitly at the top level, starting from `contents: read`, and no workflow uses write-all.

verification.note: Every workflow declares explicit permissions, blanket grants are refused, and an unexplained top-level write scope fails -- checked against this repository and against synthetic violations.

entries.failure_mode: A compromised action inherits write access to the repository.

entries.title: Third-party actions are pinned to a full commit SHA
entries.statement: No workflow references an action by tag or branch; every `uses:` names a 40-character SHA.

verification.note: Every `uses:` names a 40-hex SHA with a version comment; tags, branches, short SHAs and uncommented pins are all detected.

entries.failure_mode: A retagged action runs attacker code inside CI with the repository's secrets.

entries.title: Fork pull requests cannot reach production secrets
entries.statement: No workflow triggered by a fork pull request has access to a production secret, and this is asserted rather than assumed.

verification.note: pull_request_target is refused outright, and any stored secret reachable from a pull request must carry a fork guard; GITHUB_TOKEN is excluded because permissions bound it.

entries.failure_mode: A malicious PR prints the exchange key by editing a test.

entries.title: Release artifacts carry version, commit, lock, SBOM, hash and attestation
entries.statement: Every deployable artifact is accompanied by its provenance, and production verifies the artifact is exactly the one CI produced.

verification.note: The record is verified from the uploaded artifact, and every corruption is caught: modified bytes, missing file, undescribed extra, wrong commit, emptied field, wrong schema version.

entries.failure_mode: Nobody can prove what is running in production.

entries.title: Dependency vulnerabilities are surveilled continuously
entries.statement: Daily alerts, weekly dependency review, monthly full audit and an immediate path for a critical CVE are all configured and exercised.

verification.note: Dependabot covers pip, npm, github-actions and docker on a schedule, and the check fails when an ecosystem this repository has is missing.

entries.failure_mode: A known-exploited dependency sits in production for weeks.

entries.title: Container images run non-root with minimal capability
entries.statement: Images use a non-root user, a minimal base, a read-only filesystem where possible, dropped capabilities, no privileged mode, no host networking unless required, and resource limits -- and CI tests those properties.

verification.note: Non-root numeric user, root-owned code, multi-stage so no toolchain ships, digest-pinned slim base; CI builds the image, proves /app is unwritable under --read-only --cap-drop=ALL, and Trivy fails the job on HIGH/CRITICAL.

entries.failure_mode: A container escape becomes host root.

entries.title: A dependency update cannot become a production deployment on its own
entries.statement: Automated dependency PRs run the full quality gate and can never trigger the production workflow without the same approvals as any other change.

verification.note: The release workflow triggers only on a version tag and workflow_dispatch; push-on-branch, pull_request and schedule are all detected, including a tag trigger that also accepts branches.

entries.failure_mode: A compromised package auto-deploys itself.

entries.title: Every component failure has a declared, tested fail-safe behaviour
entries.statement: Price feed, risk engine, exchange status, analytics, model, audit, database and WebSocket each have a documented failure policy, and a test asserts the system takes it.

verification.note: Every component has a declared response, every degradation names what is lost and expires into a halt, and an undeclared component resolves to HALT_ALL rather than to carrying on.

entries.failure_mode: Fail-open is chosen by default because no one chose anything.

entries.title: Crash during a fill replays to a safe, reconciled state
entries.statement: Killing the process at each stage of an order lifecycle leaves a state the recovery path can reconcile without duplicating or losing an order.

verification.note: The process is killed at each stage of the order lifecycle; the dangerous gap (venue filled, no local record) is reported rather than averaged away, and the replay cannot double the order.

entries.failure_mode: A restart loses or doubles a live position.

entries.title: Backups are encrypted, off-host and restore-tested
entries.statement: A scheduled drill restores from backup and verifies the result; a backup that has never been restored is not counted.

verification.note: The drill measures rather than asserts: slow, stale and throwing restores each fail, and a restore that raises is a failed drill instead of a crashed drill run.

entries.failure_mode: The backup turns out to be unreadable on the day it is needed.

entries.title: RTO and RPO are declared and measured
entries.statement: Recovery time and data-loss objectives carry actual numbers chosen for this operation, and a drill measures whether they are met.

verification.note: Every data class carries a number and a justification; trade records tolerate no loss while market history tolerates a minute, and RTO is tighter with open positions than flat.

entries.failure_mode: Recovery takes longer than anyone assumed and nobody had a number to check against.

entries.title: Concurrency produces no double order, lost order or corrupted position
entries.statement: Simultaneous signals on one symbol, and an order request interleaved with disconnect, reconnect and a duplicate response, leave exactly one consistent outcome.

verification.note: Fifty coroutines race one idempotency key and exactly one wins; concurrent completion and failure cannot release a claimed key, and distinct decisions never collide into one key.

entries.failure_mode: A race doubles a position under exactly the market conditions that caused the race.

entries.title: Performance baselines exist and regressions are flagged
entries.statement: p50/p95/p99, error rate, CPU and memory baselines are recorded for feature generation, signal generation, inference, risk evaluation, order processing, database, API and WebSocket, and a large regression fails or escalates.

verification.note: Percentile budgets for the whole trading path, with a tail regression caught where a mean would hide it, and an undeclared operation raising rather than passing silently.

entries.failure_mode: The bot becomes too slow to act on its own signals and nothing says so.

entries.title: Chaos exercises end in a safe state, not merely a live process
entries.statement: Killing the database, killing the WebSocket, delaying and corrupting exchange responses, dropping packets, returning 500s and restarting mid-fill all end in the declared safe state.

verification.note: Each scenario from the source document resolves through the same policy table the runtime consults; compound failures take the strictest answer, and every bounded failure escalates.

entries.failure_mode: "It did not crash" is mistaken for "it stayed correct".

entries.title: Malformed input is rejected safely with an audit event
entries.statement: Fuzzed API payloads, market data, exchange responses, WebSocket messages, configuration, model inputs and serialised state are rejected with no state corruption, no unauthorized action, no secret leakage, and an audit record.

verification.note: Each arrow of the source document's chain is a separate assertion: rejected safely, no corrupted state, no secret leakage, audit event -- not merely 'it did not crash'.

entries.failure_mode: A malformed message leaves the system in a state no test ever described.

entries.title: Paper qualification precedes live
entries.statement: Live trading is unlocked only after the declared paper-trading qualification -- duration, sample count and performance criteria -- has been met and recorded.

verification.note: Duration, sample count and eight performance criteria, all of which must pass; the lucky fortnight fails on sample size however good its numbers, and tightening a threshold invalidates an older pass.

entries.failure_mode: A strategy meets real capital before it has ever met real conditions.

entries.title: Production is a protected GitHub environment
entries.statement: Deployment to production requires environment approval, a trusted branch, a trusted workflow and short-lived credentials; pushing to main is not sufficient.

verification.note: Every deploying job names a protected environment, promote uses the stricter one, the workflow is dispatch-only, and its token is read-only by default.

entries.failure_mode: A merge becomes a deployment with nobody deciding.

entries.title: Canary precedes full exposure
entries.statement: A new release trades at a reduced exposure with monitoring before exposure is increased; there is no paper-to-100% path.

verification.note: Promotion depends on the canary, the canary exposure is bounded at 25 percent, and promotion is skipped during a rollback drill.

entries.failure_mode: A regression meets the whole account at once.

entries.title: Automatic halt triggers are machine-enforced
entries.statement: Unexpected position, reconciliation failure, data staleness, risk-engine failure, authentication anomaly, abnormal order rate, exchange errors, crash loop, model drift and unexpected configuration change each raise an alert, a safe halt and an audit record.

verification.note: Each condition fires alone, a compound incident takes the strictest severity rather than the first match, and a trigger whose state is missing or malformed fires instead of passing.

entries.failure_mode: A human has to notice a problem that a rule could have caught in a second.

entries.title: The production startup self-test blocks live on any failure
entries.statement: Configuration, secrets, TLS, database, exchange authentication, market-data freshness, model load, risk engine, audit, kill switch, reconciliation and qualification are all checked at startup; any failure means LIVE BLOCKED.

verification.note: Debug left on, a testnet endpoint, a cleartext endpoint, a percentage where a fraction was meant, a missing secret and an unreachable kill switch each block live; an unevaluated check blocks and stays distinct from a failed one.

entries.failure_mode: The bot starts trading with a component that was never actually up.

entries.title: Configuration drift is detected and DEBUG never reaches production
entries.statement: Unexpected environment variables, risk limits, exchanges, endpoints, debug mode or authentication configuration are detected against a versioned baseline, and DEBUG=true is refused in production.

verification.note: Drift is detected in both directions -- an added key is an unreviewed setting, a removed key is a deleted control -- and debug switching on shows as drift.

entries.failure_mode: A debugging change made at 2am stays in production for a month.

entries.title: A behavioural security layer halts anomalous trading
entries.statement: Order frequency, symbol set, size, direction and time-of-day are profiled, and a sharp deviation raises a security alert and halts trading even when the credentials are valid.

verification.note: Unknown symbol, off-hours activity, bursts, sub-second intervals, outsized orders and long directional runs all halt, while a normal session does not trip the guard. The profile is declared rather than learned.

entries.failure_mode: A credential thief drains the account using perfectly valid credentials.

entries.title: Rollback is defined and exercised
entries.statement: The production workflow can return to the previous trusted artifact, and a drill proves it.

verification.note: A rollback job exists, is exercised by the drill input, verifies the running version changed, and is mutually exclusive with promotion.

entries.failure_mode: The only way out of a bad deploy is forward.

entries.title: Every production defect yields a permanent regression test
entries.statement: A defect gets a REG-#### entry, a root cause, a test that fails before the fix, and that test is never deleted because the bug is gone.

verification.note: The registry refuses a regression entry that names no test.

entries.failure_mode: The same bug ships twice.

entries.title: Every security finding yields a permanent SEC-#### test
entries.statement: A security weakness gets a SEC-#### entry and a test that would fail if the weakness returned.

verification.note: Same contract as GOV-001, applied to the security_regression kind.

entries.failure_mode: A fixed vulnerability quietly reappears in a refactor.

entries.title: Mutation testing runs nightly on the critical subsystems
entries.statement: Risk, execution, signals, position sizing and the order FSM are mutation-tested on a schedule, with per-subsystem thresholds.

verification.note: nightly-quality.yml runs one matrix job per subsystem on a schedule; a pull-request gate that slow is one that gets switched off.
The nightly workflow's own gate covers every job in it.

entries.failure_mode: Coverage is reported as quality evidence when it is not.

entries.title: No silent degradation in a security or risk path
entries.statement: A bare except, a broad exception handler, a `pass` in a critical path and a default-allow security decision are all detected by static analysis and individually reviewed.

verification.note: check_no_silent_broad_except catches the `pass` shape; check_no_default_allow_on_failure catches the worse one -- a broad except in a risk, API, security or execution module that returns a permitting value.

entries.failure_mode: A swallowed exception in the risk gate becomes a financial vulnerability.

entries.title: Requirement-to-test traceability is machine-checked
entries.statement: Every requirement names its verifying tests, those files are checked to exist at load, and the traceability document is generated rather than maintained by hand.
entries.failure_mode: The matrix says a requirement is covered by a test that was deleted last quarter.

entries.title: Serious defects get a recorded root-cause analysis
entries.statement: Each serious defect records what happened, why detection failed, why the existing control failed, why the design permitted it, and the new control that prevents recurrence.

verification.note: The template asks all five questions, refuses to stop at a person, requires the layer that should have caught it, and requires the regression test to fail against the pre-fix code.

entries.failure_mode: "Developer made a mistake" is accepted as a root cause and nothing changes.

entries.title: Quality metrics are collected and escaped defects are counted per layer
entries.statement: Pass rate, branch coverage, mutation score, regression count, escaped defects, vulnerabilities, secret incidents, MTTD, MTTR, deployment failure rate, rollback rate, recovery-test success, model drift, signal drift, data freshness and reconciliation failures are tracked.

verification.note: A metric it cannot measure is reported as unavailable with a reason rather than omitted, and zero escaped defects is stated explicitly -- 'we have not measured this' and 'this is zero' are different statements.

entries.failure_mode: Nobody can say which verification layer keeps letting defects through.

entries.title: main is protected and every required check must be green
entries.statement: Direct push, force push, CI bypass, merging a failing PR and unreviewed critical change are all refused; required checks are the workflow gates, not individual jobs.
entries.failure_mode: A required check that never reports satisfies the requirement by being absent.

entries.title: The quality maturity target is Level 5 on the trading-critical path
entries.statement: Supply-chain security, artifact provenance, cryptographic controls, continuous threat monitoring, formal traceability, mutation testing, red-team exercise and independent review all apply to the trading-critical path; non-critical utilities may sit lower, explicitly.

verification.note: Each claimed Level 5 capability names an artifact that exists on disk: supply chain, provenance, cryptographic controls, threat model, recovery, traceability and the readiness conjunction.

entries.failure_mode: Maturity is claimed globally on the strength of the easiest subsystem.

entries.title: "Production ready" is a conjunction, not a coverage number
entries.statement: Production readiness requires every mandatory test, every critical security control, no unresolved critical or high defect, risk invariants, model verification, the regression suite, the recovery test, paper qualification, artifact integrity and production approval -- all of them.

verification.note: Readiness reports blockers rather than a percentage, every critical entry must be verified, a claimed test that is missing is a blocker, and an evaluation that cannot run exits 2 rather than being folded into a failure.

entries.failure_mode: A single green percentage is mistaken for readiness.

entries.title: CI output reaching an agent is bounded at 30 lines per fetch
entries.statement: Every command that can page a file, a history or a CI log into an agent's context must carry an explicit bound of at most 30 lines, and a violation returns exactly one configured instruction line and nothing else.

verification.note: Pins the limit at the inclusive boundary -- 30 allowed, 31 refused -- and asserts the refusal is the single line read from policy, so the message and the configuration cannot drift apart.

entries.failure_mode: An unbounded log fetch exhausts the context window, and the session loses the state it needed in order to fix the failure it was reading about.

entries.title: Live CI monitoring is refused, not rate-limited
entries.statement: Following a CI run -- gh run watch, --watch, tail -f, docker or kubectl logs -f, watch -n, inotifywait -m, a while-true poll loop, or the Monitor tool -- is refused for this project regardless of what it is pointed at.

verification.note: Covers each spelling of a live watch and the Monitor tool, and asserts a bounded log fetch is still allowed, so the rule caps streams without blinding the agent to failures.

entries.failure_mode: A watch with no end emits into context for as long as CI runs, which no per-call line bound can cap.

entries.title: CI failure is pushed to the pull request, never polled for
entries.statement: Every completed run of a pull-request workflow posts a single self-updating comment naming each job that is not green -- failure, cancellation, timeout, neutral, action_required, stale, or an unexcused skip -- together with its first failing step and the exact failing lines, so no agent ever reads a run log; a green run posts nothing, and a standing notice is rewritten as recovered.

verification.note: Asserts the job carries no `if:` so every completed run is inspected, that the not-green predicate is an inverted allowlist, that its ALLOW_SKIPPED set equals the union of every gate's, that the notice carries extracted failure messages under a hard line cap, and that it updates its prior comment rather than stacking new ones.

entries.failure_mode: Without a push notice the only way to learn a pull request failed is to poll or to read logs, which is exactly what GOV-011 and GOV-012 forbid.

entries.title: Every required check also runs in the merge queue
entries.statement: A workflow that gates a pull request must also trigger on merge_group, and its gate job must not be fenced off by a pull-request-only condition, so that every check branch protection requires can report on the queue ref.

verification.note: Derives the gating set from the workflows themselves rather than restating it, so a newly added gate cannot quietly skip the merge_group requirement.

entries.failure_mode: A required check that does not run on the queue ref never reports, the entry waits for a result that cannot arrive, and the queue jams for every pull request behind it -- silently, because nothing failed.

entries.title: A pull request's wall clock is bounded by its tests, not its installs
entries.statement: Only the job that runs the test suite installs the project's runtime dependencies; jobs whose steps are stdlib-only install nothing beyond the one tool they invoke, torch is always taken from the CPU wheel index, the suite's install is cached and keyed on the requirements files, the shard count matches the declared split total, and a superseded run on a branch is cancelled.

verification.note: Asserts no stdlib-only job installs requirements.txt or torch, that the lint job reads its ruff pin from requirements-dev.txt, that the test job installs through uv with its cache enabled, that every workflow installing torch names the CPU index, that the shard list and the declared total agree, and that a new push cancels the previous run off main.

entries.failure_mode: An install added to a job that does not need it is invisible in a green run, so minutes accumulate on every pull request with nothing attributing them to the change that added them.

entries.title: A CI job installs every third-party module its own steps import
entries.statement: python-lint installs each third-party module reachable from the scripts it runs -- derived from their imports, not from a list kept by hand -- with every version read out of a requirements file rather than repeated inline.

verification.note: test_the_lint_job_installs_everything_its_steps_import walks the AST of qe_gate.py, both generate_*_docs.py and both registry modules, keeps the imports that are not stdlib, and asserts the job installs each one. Removing jsonschema from the install line fails it, which is the defect that produced the entry.

entries.failure_mode: Trimming the job to ruff alone left qe_gate without jsonschema, which it raises GateError without, and without PyYAML, which it needs to parse the workflows. The local run passed because the developer's interpreter already had both, so the gap appeared only in CI.
entries.notes: Escaped to CI, not to a running system: the gate this broke is what checks the registry, and it broke because the job stopped installing what the gate imports. It passed locally because the developer's interpreter already had jsonschema and PyYAML, so the only environment that could see it was the clean one. Filed because a green local run that is red in CI is a false green, and the rule that a defect gets a permanent test applies to those too. layer: test-suite

entries.title: A new test is written to run as fast as it can while still deciding its question
entries.statement: The suite's own running cost is budgeted and the budget only ever falls: the number of real wall-clock sleeps and process spawns in tests/ is frozen and may be lowered but never raised, no single stall exceeds 0.1s, and a budget with slack left in it fails until it is lowered so the saving is banked rather than spent.

verification.note: Counts sleeps between a scheduler yield and a cancelled-task sentinel and subprocess spawns across every test module, asserts both stay inside their frozen budgets, asserts no single stall exceeds 0.1s, and asserts each budget equals the actual count so slack cannot accumulate.

entries.failure_mode: A sleep or a spawn added to one test is imperceptible and is never attributed to the commit that added it, so the suite's cost rises monotonically and the minutes bought back by sharding are given away.

entries.title: The last manual step in the merge path presses itself, one pull request at a time
entries.statement: When main moves, exactly one open pull request -- the oldest non-draft one whose mergeable_state is `behind` -- is brought up to date, using a token whose pushes start workflow runs; a missing token fails the job rather than leaving a branch up to date with stale checks, nothing is parked, drafted or closed, and the chain continues when that pull request merges.

verification.note: Asserts it fires on a push to main and can be restarted by hand, that two runs cannot pick the same pull request, that it refuses GITHUB_TOKEN and fails before mutating anything when the PAT is absent, that it returns after one update, skips drafts, updates only a `behind` branch, retries an uncomputed mergeability, tolerates a 422 race, and parks or drafts nothing.

entries.failure_mode: A branch updated with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow run, so the pull request carries the check runs of its previous head: up to date, green-looking and permanently unmergeable -- the same trap the removed queue's promotion step fell into.

entries.title: Dependencies between src packages run downward, and the exceptions are a shrinking list
entries.statement: Every top-level package in src/ is placed in exactly one layer of config/architecture_layers.json and may import only from its own layer or a lower one; a package in no layer is a failure, each upward edge that already exists is declared with the argument for it, and an inversion that has been fixed must leave the list rather than leaving a slot for the next one.

verification.note: Pins the contract -- every package placed once, every layer and every accepted inversion carrying its argument, endpoints that exist on disk, api outermost -- and drives the rule on synthetic graphs: an upward edge is reported, a downward or same-layer one is not, an accepted one is not, a fixed one must be banked, and an unplaced package fails.
test_repository_satisfies_every_invariant runs the layering check against the live repository on every push.

entries.failure_mode: A package-level cycle never fails at import time -- it hides behind submodule and deferred imports -- and surfaces instead as two packages that cannot be changed, tested or reasoned about apart.

entries.title: CI run data is unreadable from a session under every condition
entries.statement: No CI log, job record, step annotation, artifact, cache entry or check result can be fetched from an agent session, and no output bound, filter or redirect makes it allowed. Dispatching or re-running a workflow to read its output is refused on the same footing. Enforced by common.command_schema.is_ci_log_access at both the PreToolUse hook and shell_exec.run(), with the policy file carrying the same patterns for sessions where the project is not importable.
entries.failure_mode: Context exhaustion by instalments. The prior policy capped bulk log retrieval instead of banning it -- 'the minimum number of lines that explains the failure is always permitted' -- which put the judgement in the hands of the party that wanted the lines and decayed into paging logs a few lines at a time. A bound cannot fix this because the objection is not output size: the notice comment already carries the status and the exact failing assertion, so a fetch adds nothing and costs a context window.

entries.title: One comment per commit carries the status and the exact failing lines
entries.statement: The CI notice waits until every watched workflow has completed for a commit, then posts or edits exactly one pull-request comment containing the status and, for each job that is not green, the workflow, job, conclusion, failing step and the exact failing lines extracted server-side. It posts on green as well as on failure, carries nothing beyond status and errors, and filters the runner's own exit-code epilogue out of the error text.
entries.failure_mode: A contributor or agent with no route to the cause of a red pull request. Since GOV-019 makes CI logs permanently unreadable, this comment is the only channel, so each of its failure modes is total: one comment per workflow means five to read and four chances to read a stale one; posting before every workflow finishes announces green on a commit that failed; and reporting 'Process completed with exit code 1' -- which is what the notice actually said on a failing shard of PR 313 -- names no test, no file and no assertion, leaving nothing to act on at all.

entries.title: intelligence does not import intel
entries.statement: src/intelligence/ must not import from src.intel. The adapter takes the concrete CryptoIntelligence via dependency injection, typed as Any at the analytics-layer boundary, so intelligence stays inside its layer.
entries.failure_mode: A future edit reintroduces an import of src.intel in src/intelligence/, silently reviving the intelligence->intel package edge.

entries.title: The control surface never misrepresents what it controls
entries.statement: GET /controls must label every control with the tier it belongs to -- live, static, or protected -- must derive a live control's bounds from the same Pydantic model the write endpoint validates against rather than declaring them a second time, must list every registry.EXCLUDED_PARAMS entry as read-only with the reason it cannot be tuned, and must never carry an exchange credential's value.
entries.failure_mode: The dashboard offers a control the backend will not honour. An operator who believes a slider moved a position-size cap or a drawdown halt, and is wrong, sizes real positions against a limit they think they changed.
entries.notes: The bounds rule is not hypothetical: the first draft of control_surface.py hardcoded fractions (0.001-0.50) while SetRiskControlsRequest validates percentages (0.1-50.0), so a live stop_loss_pct of 2.0 would have been reported as below its own minimum. The model is injected into build_control_surface() rather than imported, which both removes the second source of truth and keeps control_surface from importing the router that imports it. 8 live controls, 16 protected, at time of writing. layer: review

entries.title: One write endpoint, and not a second way in
entries.statement: POST /controls/{name} must route each write to the setter that already owns the control -- a risk control through the same Pydantic model POST /risk-controls validates against, a tunable through ParameterRegistry bounds -- must refuse any registry.EXCLUDED_PARAMS entry that has no operator setter with 403, and must carry the same operator_secret second factor as the endpoints it routes to.
entries.failure_mode: A unified endpoint becomes a bypass: a value the dedicated endpoint would have rejected is written through the general one, so a bound that exists in the model is not a bound that holds in production.
entries.notes: The router threads operator and operator_secret into the risk-control model rather than faking them: both are required fields, so validating with a placeholder would exercise a different model than the real endpoint does -- the exact bypass this entry forbids -- and the operator's name belongs on the write anyway. execution_mode is checked against _OPERATOR_SETTABLE before EXCLUDED_PARAMS, because it is in both and refusing it would break the one runtime switch the system documents. layer: review

entries.title: A control change is pushed, not waited for
entries.statement: A successful write through POST /controls/{name} must broadcast a control_changed frame to every connected websocket client; a rejected write must broadcast nothing; and a client that fails to receive must be dropped without failing the write or depriving the remaining clients.
entries.failure_mode: A control moved between heartbeats is invisible until the next one, so an operator moves a slider, sees nothing change, and moves it again -- or a second dashboard shows a stale value while acting on it.
entries.notes: The broadcast runs after the write has been applied, so a send failure must never surface as a failed write; dead clients are dropped instead, matching the heartbeat's own error path. The client set is snapshotted under the lock before sending, because discarding a dead client while iterating it would mutate during iteration. On the frontend the frame travels a separate channel from the tick: panels read equity_usd and positions off the tick, and pushing a control frame through setTick would blank them on every control change. layer: review

entries.title: A setting the operator changes takes effect without a restart
entries.statement: get_settings() must return the configuration in force including live operator overrides; an override must be validated by the field's own validators before it applies, must leave the previous value in force if refused, must be refused by name if the path is not a settings leaf, and must never expose a reader to a partially-rebuilt settings tree. No object may capture settings at construction.
entries.failure_mode: Every configuration value is fixed for the life of the process, so an operator reacting to live market conditions must restart the bot -- flattening positions and losing in-flight state -- to change a window length or a risk limit.
entries.notes: 79 of the 80 get_settings() calls in src/ already read at use time, so the fix was the function, not 188 fields. The cache is never cleared: VUL-028 showed that invalidating it in a request path re-instantiates every setting from the environment and exposes concurrent readers to a half-built object. The effective settings are rebuilt off the read path and the module reference is swapped, so a reader sees the whole previous object or the whole next one. Re-validation rather than model_copy(update=) is deliberate: copy runs no validators and would accept a negative kelly_multiplier. EXCLUDED_PARAMS is unchanged and still bars the autotuner from risk limits; it never described what the operator may do, and reading it that way had locked the owner out of their own position caps. Credentials remain permanently unexposed and unsettable; api.host/port/reload and the storage connection fields are reported requires_restart rather than falsely live. layer: review

entries.title: A conflict confined to generated files resolves itself, and is gated before it is pushed
entries.statement: When no open pull request is behind, the oldest conflicted non-draft pull request on a branch in this repository is merged with main; the merge is completed only if every conflicted path is a generated document with a known generator, in which case each is regenerated from the merged inputs rather than resolved to either side, and one unknown conflicted path abandons the whole merge and leaves the pull request untouched. Both the conflicted and the cleanly-merged path run the quality gate before the single push to the head branch, using the token whose pushes start workflow runs; a refused gate pushes nothing and fails the job.

verification.note: Asserts that a fork is never nominated, that nothing is nominated on a run that already updated a branch, that the job runs only on a nomination, that it uses the PAT and the whole history, that it installs nothing, that only the two generated documents are resolvable and an unknown path aborts the merge before any regeneration, that resolution regenerates rather than taking --ours or --theirs, and that there is exactly one push to the head branch and it comes after the gate.

entries.failure_mode: Every pull request that adds a registry entry regenerates the whole traceability document, so any two of them conflict regardless of how unrelated the entries are -- which made a registry entry cost a manual rebase per pull request ahead of it. The file that does not conflict is the dangerous one: git merges the registry JSON cleanly and can still produce a document the strict loader refuses, two branches allocating the same id being the usual way, since the scaffolder allocates against main and cannot see open branches. Resolving without re-running the gate would push that onto the head branch, green in appearance.

entries.title: The eighteen-engine seam is asserted from both sides, positions included
entries.statement: Every eNN_*.py module declares an _ENGINE_ID matching its filename and exposes one engine class with `async run(self, symbol, data)`; every engine given empty data abstains into a contract-valid EngineOutput rather than raising; EngineOrchestrator registers exactly eighteen engines in the order its positional attribution assumes; every engine has an SLA and every SLA an engine; and a cycle accounts for all eighteen as either an output or a named failure, each output honouring the same contract the producers were held to.

verification.note: Asserts the contract from the producer side per engine and again where the consumer receives it, pins the list order against the positional attribution in run(), and runs one real cycle to prove no engine is dropped or duplicated. Swapping two entries in the registration list fails only this test -- every other test in the suite still passes, which is why it exists.

entries.failure_mode: run() attributes result i to E-{i+1} by position, so reordering the registration list files every output under the wrong engine, applies every SLA to the wrong engine and names the wrong thing in every log line -- silently, with no exception and no failing per-engine test.

entries.title: A test's result never depends on which tests ran before it
entries.statement: Every test establishes the state it asserts on. No test reads process-global state that an earlier test left behind, so a test's result is identical under any execution order and any pytest-xdist worker assignment.

verification.note: TestEnsembleBlendPersistence pins its own blend weight rather than inheriting whatever the process-wide parameter_registry holds, and test_promoted_registry_weight_overrides_static_cfg asserts the registry overlay those tests previously depended on by accident.
Pins the overlay itself: a registered value wins over the base settings it is handed.

entries.failure_mode: Three ensemble-blend tests passed in file order and failed under pytest-xdist, because AutoTuningScheduler.start() leaves risk.ensemble_blend_weight in a process-global registry and effective_risk_settings() then overlays it on top of the config a later test set. The engine blended at 0.15 while the test had configured 0.0, and the test still reported the code it names as correct.
entries.notes: Escaped to the test suite, not to a running system: the blend weight the engine used in production was always correct, and what failed was the test's claim to have checked it. Filed as a regression anyway because the rule that a defect gets a permanent test applies to a false green as much as to a bad trade. layer: test-suite

entries.title: On-chain features never report a fabricated constant
entries.statement: SOPR, NVT and MVRV are either genuinely computed or NaN; no on-chain metric returns a finite value that varies with none of its inputs, and an RPC outage is reported as NaN rather than as a neutral-looking reading.
entries.failure_mode: A constant 1.0 SOPR reached the live feature dict in src/intel.py and was persisted to intelligence_features_history beside measured columns, so models trained and traded on a fabricated on-chain signal, and a bitcoind outage was indistinguishable from a neutral market.
entries.notes: Escaped to production: the constant reached the live feature dict in src/intel.py and was persisted to intelligence_features_history beside measured columns. The test suite could not catch it because the test that existed asserted the placeholder (== 1.0) rather than the requirement, so the layer that should have caught it is the review that accepted a return of a bare literal from a metric together with a docstring describing a computation the body never performed. layer: review

entries.title: Each pytest process owns its own DuckDB file
entries.statement: Every pytest process, controller or xdist worker, resolves DUCKDB_PATH to a file only it opens; no two processes in a run share a DuckDB database.
entries.failure_mode: Workers inherit the controller's DUCKDB_PATH, DuckDB takes an exclusive lock, and whichever worker opens the file second dies with 'Conflicting lock is held', failing a shard at random and reading as a flake.
entries.notes: Escaped to the test suite, not to a running system: production reads DUCKDB_PATH from its own environment and never had two processes sharing one file. What broke was the suite's own isolation, and only under -n, so it presented as a flake that moved between shards rather than as a defect. Filed because a red shard nobody can attribute is a false signal in the gate that merges every change. layer: test-suite

entries.title: Registry ids are allocated against every branch, not one work tree
entries.statement: The scaffolder must refuse to hand out a registry id that is already used by an entry on any other branch, and must refuse an explicitly passed id that another branch already holds.
entries.failure_mode: Two branches open at once are handed the same id; on merge two different requirements share it, or one is renumbered and a depends_on elsewhere silently points at the wrong entry.
entries.notes: Happened three times in one session (SECR-013/014 taken by two branches, then a third). Every collision was caught by hand; no check would have caught any of them. The scaffolder had tests, and they asserted that the entry it produced was schema-valid -- never that the id it chose was free anywhere but here. layer: test-suite

entries.title: The scaffolder validates with the loader the gate runs
entries.statement: qe_new_requirement.py must report success only for an entry that src.quality.registry.load_registry accepts, not merely one the JSON schema accepts.
entries.failure_mode: The scaffolder prints [ok] for an entry the gate rejects, moving the failure to CI and making an invalid entry look reviewed on the way past.
entries.notes: Observed as '[ok  ] added SEC-0001' for an entry whose test_type was 'governance', which the schema does not constrain and the loader does. Its tests asserted the scaffolder's output validated against the schema, which is the weaker of the two validators it had to satisfy. layer: test-suite

entries.title: The container image takes torch from the CPU wheel index
entries.statement: The Dockerfile must resolve torch from the CPU wheel index before it installs requirements.txt, so the image never pulls the CUDA-bundling wheel into a build layer.
entries.failure_mode: The container build job exhausts the runner's disk and dies on 'No space left on device' before the image is scanned, so the Security gate is red for a reason unrelated to the diff under review.
entries.notes: GOV-015 pinned the CPU index for every workflow that installs torch, and its test globs .github/workflows.
